title: Promotion pathways and calibration protocol
author: Priya Shah
body:
Summary:
This document defines Redwood's standardized promotion pathways and the company calibration protocol used by people managers, reviewers, and people-ops to reach consistent, equitable promotion decisions. It provides a step-by-step workflow, artifact checklist, example communication templates, and a compact rubric managers must use during promotion cycles.

Scope:
- Applies to all individual contributor (IC) and manager career ladders across engineering, product, design, SRE, and applied ML teams.
- Covers promotion recommendation, calibration meeting cadence, evidence requirements, decision recording, and appeal windows.
- Does not replace role-specific technical assessments; it supplements them with cross-functional calibration.

Principles (why this exists):
1) Fairness: ensure equivalent standards across teams and geographies.
2) Evidence-first: promotions are based on sustained impact, scope, and demonstrated behaviors.
3) Manager accountability: managers assemble and present candid evidence and development context.
4) Transparency: timelines, outcomes, and next steps are shared with the candidate and HR.

Promotion Pathways (high level):
- Time-based eligibility: minimum time-in-level is guidance (typical ~18–30 months) but not a guarantee. Exceptional cases may be escalated with supporting evidence.
- Role-driven progression: technical scope enlargement, cross-team influence, and leadership behaviors determine level change.
- Dual-track moves: for people moving from IC to manager (or vice versa), use the cross-track ramp plan (see Appendix).

Required Evidence (manager to assemble when recommending promotion):
1) Promotion packet (single PDF or Google Doc) containing:
   - 2–4 example impact narratives (what, why, measurable outcome).
   - Peer and stakeholder feedback snippets (not raw chat transcripts).
   - Recent performance review summary and 3–5 goals from last 12 months.
   - Updated role profile aligning candidate contributions to target level rubric.
2) Manager endorsement (one-page rationale) with proposed promotion effective date and compensation ask.
3) Calibration notes: list of comparable peers at target level (for context).

Calibration Protocol (step-by-step):
1) Submission window: Managers submit promotion packets during the quarterly calibration window or as approved out-of-cycle requests for critical/expedited cases.
2) Packet validation (people-ops): People-ops confirms completeness within 3 business days and returns missing items.
3) Reviewer assignment: People-ops assigns 3 reviewers: (a) direct manager’s peer, (b) cross-functional partner, (c) ladder subject matter owner. Reviewers must not be in direct reporting relationship to the candidate.
4) Asynchronous review (5 business days): Reviewers score candidate against rubric and provide written rationale. Scores: 1 (below), 2 (meets), 3 (exceeds).
5) Calibration meeting (if needed): For borderline or conflicting packets, the calibration panel (people-ops, reviewer pool, and manager) meets. Decisions are reached by consensus; people-ops facilitates final tie-break if needed.
6) Decision recording: People-ops records the outcome, rationale, and any deferral actions in the promotion registry.
7) Manager communication: Manager communicates outcome to candidate within 2 business days of final decision. People-ops coordinates compensation change and payroll actions if approved.

Scoring rubric (compact):
- Use this rubric to convert qualitative evidence into a calibration score. Managers and reviewers must cite specific artifacts for each scored dimension.

| Dimension              | 1 - Below | 2 - Meets        | 3 - Exceeds                             |
|-----------------------|-----------|------------------|-----------------------------------------|
| Impact & Results      | Local bug fixes, limited ownership | Consistent delivery of features with measurable metrics | Ownership of cross-team initiatives, measurable multi-quarter impact |
| Scope & Complexity    | Single-service scope | Multi-service or cross-team projects | Architect-level influence, long-term technical strategy |
| Leadership & Influence| Limited mentoring | Regular mentoring, effective stakeholder management | Cross-org influence, drives strategy and culture |
| Craft & Judgment      | Works within established patterns | Makes tradeoffs with sound rationale | Innovates approaches and raises team standards |
| Growth & Learnability | Little growth in year | Evidence of learning new skills | Proactive domain-building and hires/promotes others |

(Include numeric average and narrative in packet.)

Calibration meeting agenda (30–60 minutes):
1) Opening & purpose (5m) — people-ops facilitator.
2) Manager presentation (10m) — 3–5 minute impact stories.
3) Reviewer feedback (10–20m) — each reviewer summarizes score & evidence.
4) Open discussion & consensus slide (10–15m).
5) Action & next steps (5m) — record outcome, communication owner, and any development plan.

Decision outcomes and follow-ups:
- Approved: Promotion effective date set; people-ops coordinates comp and update to org systems. Manager creates a 90–180 day transition plan with role expectations.
- Deferred (development recommended): Document specific gaps, measurable objectives, and a reassessment date (typically 6 months).
- Denied (insufficient case): Manager and people-ops provide concrete next steps and timeline for reapplication (usually 12 months).

Appeals and escalation:
- Candidates may request a review within 10 business days of outcome. Appeals require new evidence or procedural concerns and are reviewed by a designated appeals panel (Head of People-ops, an HRBP, and one engineering leader not previously involved).

Manager responsibilities (checklist):
- [ ] Collect and curate 2–4 impact narratives.
- [ ] Gather peer and stakeholder feedback (minimum 3 unique sources).
- [ ] Complete the manager endorsement form.
- [ ] Share comparable peer examples for calibration context.
- [ ] Discuss promotion conversation with candidate pre-submission (transparent expectations).

People-ops responsibilities:
- Validate packets and assign reviewers within 3 business days.
- Maintain promotion registry and anonymized calibration metrics for audit.
- Facilitate calibration meeting and record final rationale.

Compensation and budgeting notes:
- Promotions are subject to budget and comp bands. People-ops will check band availability and provide guidance on market adjustments.
- Compensation increases tied to promotion follow the standard comp approval workflow (people-ops -> finance -> payroll).

Templates & communication examples:
1) Manager note (pre-submission to candidate):
"I believe you're operating at X level in these areas: [list]. I'm preparing a promotion packet to present during the next calibration window. If you have artifacts you'd like included, please share them by [date]."

2) Post-decision (approved) example:
"Congratulations — following calibration, we are promoting you to [new role] effective [date]. Next steps: people-ops will process comp changes and I'll share your 90-day transition plan."

Asynchronous and remote-specific guidance:
- For distributed teams, encourage cross-timezone reviewer assignments and rely on asynchronous evidence threads.
- People-ops will accept recorded walkthroughs (up to 10 minutes) in lieu of synchronous demos when necessary.

Frequently asked questions (short):
Q: Is time-in-role required?
A: It is guideline-based, not absolute. Exceptional impact can shorten expected timelines, but must be well-documented.

Q: Can a manager self-initiate an out-of-cycle promotion?
A: Yes for critical retention or business needs, but packets must be pre-approved by people-ops for a fast-track workflow.

Audit, tracking, and metrics to monitor:
- Quarterly promotion rate by team, level, and demographic slice (people-ops will publish anonymized dashboard).
- Average time-in-level for promotions.
- Appeal rate and resolution latency.

Appendix A: Promotion rubric mapping (example for E3 -> E4 engineer)
| Competency Area | E3 expectations (examples) | E4 expectations (examples) |
|-----------------|----------------------------|----------------------------|
| Ownership       | Owns feature area and fixes bugs end-to-end | Owns cross-service initiative, defines requirements, and coordinates releases |
| System Design   | Contributes to design discussions | Leads design for components with clear tradeoffs and docs |
| Mentorship      | Helps onboard peers | Actively mentors multiple teammates, influences hiring bar |

Appendix B: Quick checklist (to paste in PRs or calendar invite)
- Packet uploaded to HR drive.
- Manager endorsement attached.
- 3 reviewer invites sent.
- Candidate pre-brief done.

Document governance:
- Owner: People-ops (Priya Shah).
- Review cadence: annual or after significant policy change.
- Next scheduled review: 2027-01-15.
